subheadline: I architect the integrations enterprises run on: e-invoicing compliance, ERP, and the LLM services that make them work without a human in the loop.

about.heading: an even
paragraphs: I have spent the last five years on the seams between systems: e-invoicing compliance platforms, ERP tools, and the microservices and message queues that keep them in agreement. Most of my work is backend and integration engineering: REST APIs, event-driven pipelines, and the unglamorous infrastructure that decides whether a product feels fast or feels broken.

Lately that has meant putting large language models somewhere they have to be reliable. I have built RAG services that pull invoices out of Sage and QuickBooks, map them to compliance schemas, and catch the anomalies before a tax authority does, and multi-LLM orchestration that has to reach a consensus before it moves anyone's money.

A lot of the rest is legacy modernisation: taking something business-critical nobody wants to touch, carving it into services with clear boundaries, and migrating the data without losing a transaction. Outside of shipping, I mentor engineers and have led a 7-person team.
